notes.text: **[Mishnah Demai 4:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Demai.4.1)** — הלוקח פרות ממי שאינו נאמן על המעשרות ושכח לעשרן, ושואלו בשבת, יאכל על פיו. חשכה מוצאי שבת, לא יאכל עד שיעשר. One who bought produce from someone not trusted on tithes and forgot to tithe it may ask him on Shabbat and eat on his word; once Shabbat is over he may not eat until he tithes. The Mishnah gives only the ruling; the words Rav Tzadok quotes, “the awe of Shabbat is upon him,” are the Yerushalmi's reason for it (next note). *Mafteach: missing*

**[Jerusalem Talmud Demai 4:1:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Demai.4.1.2)** — רִבִּי בִּיבִי בְשֵׁם רִבִּי חֲנִינָא: אֵימַת שַׁבָּת עָלָיו וְהוּא אוֹמֵר אֱמֶת. R. Bivi in the name of R. Chanina: the awe of Shabbat is upon him, so he tells the truth. The Yerushalmi also gives a second reason (“they permitted it out of respect for Shabbat”); Rav Tzadok builds the whole os on the first: on Shabbat even an am ha'aretz is afraid to lie. *Mafteach: found*

**[Berakhot 57b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.57b.13)** — שבת אחד מששים לעולם הבא. Shabbat is one-sixtieth of the World to Come. Rav Tzadok does not name the source; this is the Gemara behind “Shabbat is a semblance of the World to Come.” *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Berakhot 56b; correct: Berakhot 57b)*

**[Vayikra Rabbah 26:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.26.7)** — אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כַּד הֲוֵינָא גַּבָּךְ הֲוֵינָא בְּעוֹלָם דְּשֶׁקֶר, וַהֲוֵית שְׁמִיעַ מִנִי מִלִּין שִׁקְרִין, דַּהֲוֵינָא דָחֵיל מִנָּךְ דְּלָא תִקְטֵילוּנְנִי; וְכַדּוּן דַּאֲנָא בְּעוֹלָם דְּקוּשְׁטָא, לֵית אַתְּ שְׁמִיעַ מִנִּי אֶלָּא מִלִּין דִּקְשׁוֹט. Shmuel, raised from the dead, tells Shaul: when I was with you I was in a world of falsehood and you heard false words from me, because I feared you would kill me; now that I am in the world of truth you hear only true words from me. Rav Tzadok's “etc.” passes over Shmuel's admission that he spoke falsely out of fear. The same exchange appears in **[Midrash Tanchuma, Emor 2:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma,_Emor.2.1)**. *Mafteach: found*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 63:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.63.8)** — וַיִּקְרְאוּ שְׁמוֹ עֵשָׂו, הֵא שָׁוְא שֶׁבָּרָאתִי בְּעוֹלָמִי. “They named him Esav”: here is the vanity I created in My world. The Midrash reads עשו as הא שוא, and Rav Tzadok takes שָׁוְא as falsehood, the stuff of this world. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Bereshit Rabbah 63:10; correct: Bereshit Rabbah 63:8)*

**[Micah 7:20](https://www.sefaria.org/Micah.7.20)** — תתן אמת ליעקב חסד לאברהם אשר נשבעת לאבתינו מימי קדם. “Grant truth to Jacob, kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from days of old.” Truth is Yaakov's trait, and so his portion is the World to Come, the world of truth. *Mafteach: wrong label (index: chapter 6; key Micah 7:20 is right)*

**[Midrash Tanchuma, Vayetzei 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma,_Vayetzei.1.1)** — הַהוֹרֵג נֶפֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָה, גּוֹלֶה לְעָרֵי מִקְלָט ... וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ גָּלָה לְחָרָן, בּוֹרֵחַ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ, וְנִתְיָרַא שֶׁלֹּא יַהֲרֹג אוֹתוֹ הָרָשָׁע עֵשָׂו אָחִיו. מִכֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאָהוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּצָרָה גְּדוֹלָה נִגְלָה עָלָיו בַּחֲלוֹם. The unwitting killer goes into exile to the cities of refuge; Yaakov went into exile to Charan, fleeing for his life, afraid that Esav would kill him; seeing him in great distress, God appeared to him in a dream. Rav Tzadok's first “etc.” passes over the list of the six cities; his second passes over the stated object of Yaakov's fear, “that the wicked Esav would kill him.” *Mafteach: found*

**[Genesis 3:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.3.4)** — ויאמר הנחש אל האשה לא מות תמתון. “The serpent said to the woman: You will surely not die.” This is the lie through which, as Rav Tzadok says, the serpent brought death into the world; the Zohar he cites at [3.4] calls the serpent's curses “the lying lip” (**[Zohar, Toldot 18:138](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Toldot.18.138)**). The print reads השפת שקר with the article on a construct; the phrase is שפת שקר of Psalms 120:2. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 63:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.63.13)** — אם לא דם שנאת ודם ירדפך ... רבנן אמרי: שנאת דמו של אדם בגופו. On Yechezkel 35:6, “Surely you have hated blood,” said of Esav: the Rabbis say, you hated a man's blood in his body. “There” refers to parashah 63 cited at [1.22]. Rav Tzadok reads it as the kelipah of murder, so lying and killing are one trait. *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar I 241b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayechi.66.672)** (Vayechi) — הִיא בָּעַאת סִימָנָא דְחַיֵּי ... וַאֲמָרָה, סִימָנָא דְחַיֵּי לָא שַׁרְיָיא, אֶלָא בְּאוֹת אֱמֶת, וּמַאי אִיהוּ אוֹת אֱמֶת, דָּא אָת ו'. Rachav asked for “a sign of life,” and a sign of life rests only on “a true sign,” which is the letter vav. The phrase סימנא דחיי is from this passage, which itself refers to the beginning of Vayikra (next note). *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zohar III 2a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayikra.1.5)** (Vayikra) — וְכֵן בְּרָחָב מַה כְּתִיב, וּנְתַתֶּם לִי אוֹת אֱמֶת, דָּא אָת ו', דְּדָא אִקְרֵי אוֹת אֱמֶת. On Rachav's request (Joshua 2:12), “give me a true sign”: this is the letter vav, which is called the sign of truth. Yaakov, the middle line, is the chariot of the vav, so truth and life belong to him, while falsehood and murder belong to Esav. *Mafteach: found*

**[Genesis 3:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.3.12)** — ויאמר האדם האשה אשר נתתה עמדי הוא נתנה לי מן העץ ואכל. “The woman You gave to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate.” Rav Tzadok does not name a source; he reads Adam's “and I ate” as an admission, unlike Kayin's denial at [2.37]. Bereshit Rabbah 19:12 reads the same answer harshly (Adam blamed God), so this is Rav Tzadok's own reading. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Genesis 4:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.4.9)** — ויאמר ה' אל קין אי הבל אחיך ויאמר לא ידעתי השמר אחי אנכי. “Where is Hevel your brother?” — “I do not know; am I my brother's keeper?” Kayin answered God with a lie. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Genesis 30:9; correct: Genesis 4:9)*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 22:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.22.13)** — ויצא קין מלפני ה', מהיכן יצא? רבי יודן בשם רבי איבו אמר: הפשיל דברים לאחוריו ויצא כגונב דעת העליונה. “Kayin went out from before Hashem”: he threw the words behind his back and went out like one who deceives the Mind on High. The same passage goes on to say that Kayin told Adam, “I did teshuvah and was pardoned.” *Mafteach: found*

**[Midrash Tanchuma, Bereshit 9:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma,_Bereshit.9.7)** — אָמַר לוֹ קַיִן: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, לֹא יָדַעְתִּי וְלֹא רָאִיתִי הָרוּג מִיָּמַי, וְכִי הָיִיתִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֲנִי מַכֵּהוּ בָאֶבֶן וְהוּא מֵת! הֱשִׁיבוֹ מִיָּד: אָרוּר אַתָּה מִן הָאֲדָמָה. Kayin pleaded that he had never seen a dead man and did not know a stone would kill; God at once answered with the curse of the ground and exile. Rav Tzadok's “etc.” passes over God's answer; for him the plea of ignorance is what made Kayin's sentence that of an unwitting killer. *Mafteach: found*

**[Genesis 4:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.4.12)** — כי תעבד את האדמה לא תסף תת כחה לך נע ונד תהיה בארץ. “When you till the ground it will no longer yield its strength to you; a wanderer and a fugitive shall you be in the land.” Exile is the punishment of the one who killed unintentionally. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zohar I 143a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Toldot.18.137-138)** (Toldot) — דְּהֲוָה יַעֲקֹב בְּעָאקוּ סַגִּי, דְּדָחִיל דְּאֲבוֹי יְדַע לֵיהּ ... כְּדֵין אָמַר, אֶל יְיָ בַּצָּרָתָה לִי קָרָאתִי וַיַּעֲנֵנִי. יְיָ הַצִּילָה נַפְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת שֶׁקֶר מִלָּשׁוֹן רְמִיָה, דָּא הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְעֵשָׂו שַׁרְיָא בֵּיהּ, דְּאִיהוּ שְׂפַת שֶׁקֶר. Yaakov was in great distress, afraid his father would recognize him; then he said Psalm 120. “The lying lip” is the level of Esav, the lie the serpent used to bring curses on the world. Sefaria marks the start of daf 143a inside 18:137, so the reference (part 1, 143a) is right. *Mafteach: found*

**[Psalms 120:1-2](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms.120.1-2)** — שיר המעלות אל ה' בצרתה לי קראתי ויענני. ה' הצילה נפשי משפת שקר מלשון רמיה. “To Hashem in my distress I called and He answered me. Hashem, rescue my soul from a lying lip, from a deceitful tongue.” The print joins אלה' for אל ה' (see the translator's note). Rav Tzadok quotes the verses again at [4.1]–[4.3] as Yaakov's own prayer. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Yevamot 65b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.65b.7)** — מותר לו לאדם לשנות בדבר השלום, שנאמר: אביך צוה וגו׳ כה תאמרו ליוסף. A person may deviate from the truth for the sake of peace, as Yosef's brothers did. Rav Tzadok does not name the source of the rule. The Mafteach points to **[Bamidbar Rabbah 11:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Bamidbar_Rabbah.11.7)**: גדול השלום שהקדוש ברוך הוא שנה בדבר מפני השלום (on Genesis 18:13). *Mafteach: found*

**Sefer Chassidim** — Not found. The words Rav Tzadok attributes to it, that one may say “a statement that can be understood two ways” (מלתא דמשתמעא לתרי אפי), did not turn up in the Sefer Chassidim text on Sefaria or in the local collections. The siman the poskim cite on deviating for peace is **[Sefer Chasidim 426](https://www.sefaria.org/Sefer_Chasidim.426)** (Magen Avraham 156:2): כי מה שאמרו שמותר לשנות בדברי שלום, זהו כשכבר עבר הדבר. It limits the permission to things already done; it does not speak of double meanings. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Rashi on Genesis 27:19](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Genesis.27.19)** — אנכי עשו בכורך: אָנֹכִי הַמֵּבִיא לְךָ וְעֵשָׂו הוּא בְּכוֹרֶךָ. Rashi divides Yaakov's words: “I am the one bringing [it] to you, and Esav is your firstborn.” This is the statement “that can be understood two ways” of [3.15]. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zohar I 143a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Toldot.19.139)** (Toldot) — כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר לִפְנֵי יְיָ, בְּהַהִיא שַׁעְתָּא אִזְדַּעְזַע כָּרְסֵי יְקָרָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, אָמְרָה: וּמַה דְּיִפּוּק חִוְיָא מֵאִינוּן לְוָוטִין, וְיִשְׁתָּאַר יַעֲקֹב בְּהוּ. When Yitzchak said he would bless Esav “before Hashem,” the Throne of Glory shook: shall the serpent come out of its curses and Yaakov be left in them? Two paragraphs later (**[Zohar, Toldot 19:141](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Toldot.19.141)**) the Zohar says: אֲתָא יַעֲקֹב בְּחָכְמָה וְאַטְעֵי לְאֲבוּי, בְּגִין לְאַיְיתָאָה בִּרְכָאן עַל עַלְמָא — Yaakov misled his father with wisdom to bring blessing to the world, measure for measure against the serpent. *Mafteach: found*

**[Berakhot 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.17a.2)** — רבון העולמים, גלוי וידוע לפניך שרצוננו לעשות רצונך, ומי מעכב? שאור שבעסה ושעבוד מלכיות. Master of the world, You know that our will is to do Your will; what holds us back? The leaven in the dough and the subjugation to the kingdoms. Rav Tzadok (“as we have said”) joins the two: subjugation comes through a trace in the heart of the nation that rules. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Sanhedrin 97a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.97a.6-7)** — זִימְנָא חֲדָא אִיקְּלַעִי לְהָהוּא אַתְרָא, וְקוּשְׁטָא שְׁמֵיהּ, וְלָא הֲווֹ מְשַׁנֵּי בְּדִיבּוּרַיְיהוּ, וְלָא הֲוָה מָיֵית אִינִישׁ מֵהָתָם בְּלָא זִימְנֵיהּ ... אֲמַרִי לַהּ: לֵיתַהּ הָכָא. שְׁכִיבוּ לֵיהּ תְּרֵין בְּנֵיהּ ... בְּמָטוּתָא מִינָּךְ, פּוֹק מֵאַתְרִין וְלָא תְּגָרֵי בְּהוּ מוֹתָנָא בְּהָנָךְ אִינָשֵׁי. In a town called Kushta (“Truth”) no one lied and no one died before his time. Rav Tavut said his wife was not home, out of modesty, and his two sons died; the townspeople asked him to leave so as not to bring death upon them. Rav Tzadok's point: even a permitted deviation from truth, in a place of truth, brought death and exile. *Mafteach: found*

**[Berakhot 55a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.55a.16)** — כשם שאי אפשר לבר בלא תבן, כך אי אפשר לחלום בלא דברים בטלים. Just as there is no grain without straw, there is no dream without idle matters (R. Yochanan in the name of R. Shimon bar Yochai, on Jeremiah 23:28). *Mafteach: missing*

**[Genesis 28:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.28.13)** — והנה ה' נצב עליו ויאמר אני ה' אלהי אברהם אביך ואלהי יצחק. “And behold, Hashem stood over him and said: I am Hashem, God of Avraham your father and God of Yitzchak.” Yaakov's dream was God Himself speaking, with nothing idle in it. *Mafteach: found*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 67:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.67.4)** — בָּא אָחִיךָ בְּמִרְמָה, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בָּא בְּחָכְמַת תּוֹרָתוֹ. “Your brother came with guile”: R. Yochanan said, he came with the wisdom of his Torah. *Mafteach: wrong label (index: parashah 66; key Bereshit Rabbah 67:4 is right)*

**[Genesis 27:35](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.27.35)** — ויאמר בא אחיך במרמה ויקח ברכתך. “He said: Your brother came with guile and took your blessing.” Yitzchak's words to Esav, which the Midrash in the previous note rereads as praise. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Yoma 83b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.83b.12-13)** — רַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא אַשְׁלֵים לֵיהּ כִּיסֵיהּ, אֲזַל אוֹתְבֵיהּ בֵּי קִיבְרֵיהּ דַּאֲבוּהּ. אִתְחֲזִי לֵיהּ בְּחֶלְמֵיהּ: תָּא שְׁקֵיל כִּיסָא דְּמַנַּח אַרֵישָׁא דְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא. לִמְחַר אֲמַר לְהוּ ... אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֶלְמָא דְּבֵי שִׁמְשֵׁי לֵית בְּהוּ מַמָּשָׁא. R. Meir would not leave his purse with the innkeeper Kidor, whose name marked him as wicked, and hid it at the grave of the man's father. In a dream the innkeeper was told to take the purse lying at that man's head. When he told them, they said: dreams of bei shimshei have no substance. Rav Tzadok's reading at [5.26]–[5.29], that the dream came from the father's spirit, rests on this detail: the purse was hidden in the father's grave. *Mafteach: found*

**[Rashi on Yoma 83b](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Yoma.83b.13.1)** — דבי שמשי: של ערבי שבתות. לית בהו ממשא: מתוך שאדם במנוחה מהרהר ורואה חלומות, ומתכון היה לדחותו שלא ילך ויטלנו. Bei shimshei means Friday nights; such dreams lack substance because a resting person muses and dreams. Rashi adds that R. Meir meant to put the man off so he would not go and take it. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Berakhot 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.55b.15)** — רבא רמי: כתיב בחלום אדבר בו, וכתיב וחלמות השוא ידברו. לא קשיא: כאן על ידי מלאך, כאן על ידי שד. Rava set the verses against each other: one dream comes through an angel, the other through a demon. Rav Tzadok writes “Berachos, there,” after citing 55a at [4.20]; the contradiction itself is on 55b. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Numbers 12:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Numbers.12.6)** — ויאמר שמעו נא דברי אם יהיה נביאכם ה' במראה אליו אתודע בחלום אדבר בו. “If there is a prophet among you, I make Myself known to him in a vision; in a dream I speak with him.” *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zechariah 10:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Zechariah.10.2)** — כי התרפים דברו און והקוסמים חזו שקר וחלמות השוא ידברו הבל ינחמון. “For the teraphim spoke iniquity, the diviners saw falsehood, and dreams speak vanity; they comfort in vain.” *Mafteach: missing*

**[Maharsha, Chiddushei Aggadot on Yoma 83b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chidushei_Agadot_on_Yoma.83b.6)** — לפי מה שאמרו פרק הרואה דחלום אמתי הוא על ידי מלאך וחלום של שקר הוא על ידי שד, ואם כן זה החלום בודאי לא היה על ידי מלאך להודיע לבנו שיגנוב כיס זה של רבי מאיר, וזה החלום על ידי השד נמי אינו, שהרי אמת היה. The Maharsha's question is exactly as Rav Tzadok reports it. His answer is different: the dream followed the man's own thoughts, since all day he had been plotting how to get R. Meir's money. Rav Tzadok answers instead that the father's spirit counseled him. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Toldot 6](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Toldot_6) (Rav Tzadok) — The same materials: Bereshit Rabbah's “with the wisdom of his Torah,” Micah's “truth to Yaakov,” Zohar I 143a on the lying lip, and Esav as הא שוא. It adds the reason: against the serpent's crookedness Yaakov had to go with ערמה, “with the crooked deal crookedly,” so his guile was itself truth. *checked*

**Parallels:** [Sod Yesharim, Sukkot 57](#/read/Sod_Yesharim,_Sukkot_57) (Ishbitz–Radzin) — Reads the same Zohar (I 143a) on Psalm 120 and also asks whether Yaakov's “I am Esav your firstborn” was a lie. It answers differently: there was no deceitful tongue in it at all, since Yaakov includes and surrounds Esav, and so he said it “in absolute truth” (באמת לאמיתו). *checked*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Pesach 44:3](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Pesach_44:3) (Rav Tzadok) — Probably what “as we have said” refers to: the same Berakhot 17a, read as one thing, “because evil is found in the nations, leaven in the dough enters the heart of Israel too” (שע"י שנמצא רע באו"ה נכנס גם בלב ישראל שאור שבעיסה). It adds the link to the yetzer called ערל. *checked*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Yismach Moshe, Vayetzei 2:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Yismach_Moshe,_Vayetzei.2.1)** (Chassidus) — Asks Rav Tzadok's question about the same Tanchuma. It also answers that Yaakov judged himself an unwitting killer, but for a different fault: to a tzaddik a light sin weighs like a heavy one, and he had caused Esav to plan murder, so he took exile on himself as atonement.
והצדיק שהקלה דומה עליו כחמורה, ודאי בעיניו יחשב כהורג נפש בשוגג ממש

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Shem MiShmuel, Vayetzei 9:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shem_MiShmuel,_Vayetzei.9.3)** (Chassidus) — Opens with the same Tanchuma and the same question. It answers through Adam's sin: Yaakov had to scour away Adam's share in bloodshed, and his exile was the matching suffering. Rav Tzadok's answer works through falsehood instead.
ויש להבין מה ענין גלות הרוצח לערי מקלט לגלות יעקב אבינו לחרן

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Cheshbon HaNefesh 136:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Cheshbon_HaNefesh.136.2)** (Mussar) — R. Mendel of Satanov raises the same proof, Yaakov's “I am Esav your firstborn,” for statements that can be understood two ways. He treats it as an objection to answer, holding that such speech is still to be avoided; Rav Tzadok treats it as the permitted path that Yaakov took.
ז"ל המקשה מלישנא דמשתמע לתרי אפי, והלא מצינו אצל יעקב שאמר אנכי עשו בכרך

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Ketem Paz on Zohar 142b:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketem_Paz_on_Zohar.142b.7)** (Kabbalah) — R. Shimon Lavi on the same Zohar passage: “rescue my soul from a lying lip” cannot mean Yaakov's own words, since he meant “I am the one bringing [it], and Esav is your firstborn.” He refers it to the serpent's level in Esav, as Rav Tzadok does before turning to Yaakov's later fear.
שאין הכונה כפי הנראה שיצילהו ממה שאמר דברי שקר לאביו אנכי עשו בכרך
